text: 'Absorbed in favour all divine' (hymn No 116). You get some impression that David had that when he went in and sat before Jehovah; he had a sense of how large God's thoughts were compared with his thoughts: "thou hast spoken of thy servant's house for a great while to come", 1 Chron 17: 17. I think what you say is good, that we become absorbed with the Person and we find that He has thought about us before time began and has destined us for glory, and to be held in glory in suited relationship with Himself.

paragraphs.speaker: DAB
text: It has been remarked as to the scripture in Ephesians, "the earnest of our inheritance" (chap 1: 14), that the Earnest we have is greater than the inheritance itself. I wondered if that showed that while the inheritance might relate from our side to the sphere of bliss into which we are brought, the Spirit gives us title to sonship, which is something for God and is in answer to God's desires.

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: Yes, I think that is full of interest, that we have that now. As remarked already, what we touch in the service of God is linked on with the rapture. There are eternal things tasted to create an appetite in us, to give us to be what we have said, absorbed with divine Persons. What an occupation! to be there at home, absorbed with the Father, absorbed with Christ.

paragraphs.speaker: DAB
text: The greatest things we have are what we are for God.

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: Indeed, that is the Spirit's mission; it is what He has come to do, to create affections that are suitable to God but to bring in persons. "We have access to the Father". The idea of access is like coming into a new country, surveying that vista in all its glory and splendour. It fills us with a sense of divine majesty, and yet we are held sustained in divine power to be at home in it.

paragraphs.speaker: ECB
text: We should understand that remark just quoted because the basis of it is that a divine Person is always greater than any inheritance, and it is the Spirit who is the Earnest.

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: So that it connects with what we have come to - to Jesus, to God: we have come to divine Persons (see Heb 12: 23,24). The inheritance is the area in which we know Them, but what we know is the Persons Themselves. We have access to the Father.

paragraphs.speaker: ECB
text: What Mr Byng said is parallel to that. You cry, Abba, Father. You are just engaged with the Father for what He is in Himself, greater than any inheritance.

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: Yes, that develops sonship's feelings in us, does it not? We are absorbed with the Father. Think of being absorbed with Him! We think of our blessings, and when we are younger they loom large; how wonderful spiritual blessings are! but they only serve as an area in which we are brought to know divine Persons. We have access to the Father, a Person, a Person well-known in grace. We sometimes sing 'Well known in Jesus' love' (hymn No 72), but we are brought to be before Him suitably, and sustained before Him in the Spirit's power. These things would help us as to what we remarked yesterday, they would enrich us in our worship to the Spirit.

paragraphs.speaker: CRB
text: Several of the doxologies refer to 'only God', - "the only wise God" (Rom 16: 27), "only Ruler", 1 Tim 6: 15. Does that connect with what we are saying?

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: Well, say some more.

paragraphs.speaker: CRB
text: You are just so taken up with divine Persons, God Himself, that you are conscious that there is noone else to be occupied with, you might say. I say that reverently. He is the only God.

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: That is very fine; it will be our eternal occupation to be occupied with God. Well, the Spirit of his Son in our hearts, having access by one Spirit: think of a divine Person being on our side, to use that expression, that we are not lost but are held at home as occupied with God.

paragraphs.speaker: EP
text: Would "the Spirit of his Son" bring in intelligence in relation to that love, and sensitiveness too?

paragraphs.speaker: RT
text: Yes, you cannot think of any disparity there, any weakness or failure or short-coming. The response, it has been remarked, will be equal to the revelation. What has been revealed is treasured in the Spirit. What shone out in Christ in His manhood is treasured by the Spirit and wrought out in the saints so that it is held in relation to the divine pleasure and will be eternally. These things should quicken our affections.
I think that the Spirit is specially occupied in quickening our affections and that produces formation with us.

paragraphs.text: One of the many and precious promises in the Bible is that all who are drawn to Jesus will be taught by God Himself, so that we often speak of the 'School of God'. All believers are in it and the Scripture tells us as to the children that they shall have great peace there. Think of being always happy in school! I recall hearing that a little boy just starting at school, when asked what class he was in, said 'The class where you have to learn to sit still'. To trust quietly in God is something that we all need to learn better. If we put our faith in Him as the Children of Israel did at the Red Sea we shall prove His salvation.

Learning one lesson leads to another so that by trusting God we get to know Him better and discover the varied glories of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. When He searches the consciences and hearts of believers it is in order that we should trace His own work in us. In this way the scripture is proved that God's people should know Him "in themselves", from the little one - indeed from the least - even to the greatest.

Then as we know Him better we learn to think less of ourselves. A little girl noticed once how small some men looked as they were working at the top of a skyscraper and said , 'They won't amount to much when they get to heaven, will they?' The fact is that we all as believers will then have left behind the old selfish - and often naughty - self, and only Christ will be seen in us. In this way, however, we shall actually 'amount to much' because just as one star differs from another in glory so we shall shine as heavenly ones, distinct from one another.

Scripture shows that the young ones can be very early taught to praise the Lord. An example of this was when the children cried "Hosanna" in the presence of Jesus in the temple. The word they used showed that they rejoiced in Him as Saviour. They may of course have learned it through their elders who had been crying the same thing as Jesus entered into the city of Jerusalem. But the Lord showed to the proud unbelievers that even these children and infants had learned perfectly a lesson which they themselves had not learned at all. Do you find that the more you say 'Hosanna', or 'Save now', the more you can say 'Hallelujah' - 'Praise the Lord'?
